title: Product Without Overflow
hints: In which type is the multiplication *performed*? `a` and `b` are both `int`, so `a * b` is computed as a 32-bit `int`. Only the finished (already overflowed) result is widened to `long long` on the way out of `return`.

Casting the result is too late: `static_cast<long long>(a * b)` still multiplies in `int`, and so does `long long r = a * b;`. Cast one *operand*; the other is promoted to match and the multiplication itself happens in 64 bits.
